verdicts.statement: Ancient Greek theatres had tall, arched entrances called parodoi or eisodoi.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that Greek theatres had tall arched entrances called parodoi or eisodoi.

verdicts.statement: Actors and chorus members entered and exited the orchestra through the parodoi or eisodoi.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly identifies the parodoi or eisodoi as the entrances through which actors and chorus members entered and exited the orchestra.

verdicts.statement: Ancient Greek theatres had a back wall called the skênê.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly describes the skênê as the back wall of Greek theatres.

verdicts.statement: The skênê reached a height of two stories by the end of the fifth century BC.
verdicts.reason: The context states that by the end of the fifth century BC, the skênê was two stories high.

verdicts.statement: The upper story of the skênê was called the episkenion.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that the upper story was called the episkenion.

verdicts.statement: Some ancient Greek theatres had a raised speaking platform in the orchestra called the logeion.
